_comment: Ceilings for everything a session loads BEFORE it does any work, in tokens
(rough: words x 1.3, tools/build_views.py:_approx_tokens). One registry so
no cap is declared twice -- registry-source-of-truth. Practice:
A ceiling is a watermark, not an endorsement: each was set at the measured
size when the surface was last reviewed, rounded up for headroom, so it can
be ratcheted DOWN by a reduction pass and never drifts up unnoticed. Raising
one is a decision somebody makes on purpose, in a commit, with the reason in
'why'. Never raise it to make a red check green.

AGENTS.md.why: Set at 19000 against a tree 14 commits stale, then re-measured on the merged tree at 19687 -- the growth is one freshness-guard gotcha added upstream the same day. Raised once, after the review the rule asks for rather than instead of it: the gotchas section is 10,494 of the total, and every entry very_deep_check.py flagged as claiming its own trap settled was read and still bites, so nothing was archived. The next raise should come with a reduction pass, not another re-measurement. 2026-09-11, later the same day: adding generated-edit-goes-upstream put the file at 20,048 and the ceiling was NOT raised. The reduction pass the clause asks for found one entry whose central claim had gone false -- the timezone-diagnosis entry called settings.local.json's env block inert, which the commit-identity entry beside it contradicts from a same-day measurement -- and moved it to record/GOTCHAS_ARCHIVE.md entry 31 in full. Measured 19,922 after. 2026-09-11, later still: the clean-session practice took the file to 20,235 and the ceiling was again NOT raised. The reduction pass compressed the verify_harness fixture-credential entry -- three variables, all three now scrubbed at the head of the harness and held there by a control, so only a NEW variable can bite -- to record/GOTCHAS_ARCHIVE.md entry 32 in full, keeping the symptom, the way to tell inheritance from absence, and the generalization live. Measured 19,753 after. 2026-09-13: spawn-session's wake-first amendment took the file over at 20,124 and the ceiling was again NOT raised. Two reductions, in order: the new paragraph itself was cut to its claim, dropping the origin story that the practice's own Story already holds in full; then the git-clone-without---branch gotcha was compressed to the symptom, the lesson and the pin. That one was already archived as record/GOTCHAS_ARCHIVE.md entry 36, whose own verdict says the live entry should keep the incident short and the lesson in full -- it had never actually been shortened, so this pass did what the archive already claimed. Measured 19,986 after. 2026-09-13, later: one quick-index row for spec/SOURCE_SET_PROSE_GAP.md took the file to 20,040 and the ceiling was again NOT raised. The reduction pass compressed the declared-hooks-exist gotcha -- its wrong-inference symptom kept, its story dropped to record/GOTCHAS_ARCHIVE.md entry 37, where it already sat in full -- on the ground that BOTH halves are mechanical now, so a session meets this as a failing check rather than as a reading it has to get right unaided. Measured 19935 after. 2026-09-13, later still: a ninth command (`vocabulary`), the `Approved` trigger on go-merge and the seeded merge authorization on spawn-session together added about 370 tokens, and the ceiling was again NOT raised. The reduction pass took out duplicated HISTORY rather than any rule: the go-merge promotion story, the `merge-authorization-keyword` reversal and the session-that-went-asking incident all sit in full in practices/go-merge.md's own Story, and the same for park-it's repo-local day, spawn-session's rename, plain-words' coining thread and decision-strength's no-backfill reasoning. Nothing a session would hit today moved. Measured 19,986 after.

CLAUDE.md.why: An @AGENTS.md include. Anything more than a line or two here is content that belongs in the file it includes.

.precedent/SESSION_PRACTICES.md.why: Generated at session start from the team and individual sources, so it varies with what resolved; the ceiling is the whole of what those sources may add to every session here.
